headline: India Crosses 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses in Less Than Nine Months
subheadline: The national campaign has reached nearly 87% of its target cohort of 14-year-old girls, with six states reporting full coverage of their identified populations.
body:
• India has administered more than 1 crore HPV vaccine doses in less than nine months under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign, reaching nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of about 1.2 crore 14-year-old girls.
  • The vaccine is free, single-dose and voluntary, given with parental consent at designated government health facilities; six states — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar — have covered 100% of their identified target populations.
  • Uttar Pradesh leads in absolute numbers with over 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh).
  • For parents: a 14-year-old daughter who has not yet been vaccinated can be registered and booked through the U-WIN platform or at the nearest designated government health facility.

India has crossed 1 crore doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare announced on November 21, a milestone in the country's effort to prevent cervical cancer. The doses were given under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched in February 2026 and which offers a free, single-dose vaccine to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities, with parental consent.

The campaign has reached nearly 87% of its identified annual target cohort of approximately 1.2 crore girls, a figure based on the Registrar General of India's 2021 population estimates, according to the ministry's press release. Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda, in a post on X, congratulated the states that have completed coverage of their target populations and noted that 12 states have crossed the 80% mark.

Six states at full coverage

Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar have each vaccinated 100% of their identified target populations. Among the other high performers, Assam has recorded 95.63% coverage, Telangana 95.28%, Karnataka 93.16% and Uttarakhand 90.17%, while Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan have crossed 80%. In absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with over 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with over 7.75 lakh.

The ministry credited coordination between the Union health ministry and state and union territory governments, district administrations, and frontline workers including ASHAs and ANMs, along with school teachers and medical specialists who worked on parental awareness. State-led initiatives in Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Sikkim were integrated into the national campaign, the release said.

How the campaign runs

The programme runs on the U-WIN digital platform, which handles real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking, vaccination slot booking and digital certificates. Programme managers use district-level data from the platform to identify coverage gaps and girls who have not yet been vaccinated. All sessions are held at designated government facilities under the supervision of trained medical officers, and vaccination sites are linked to 24x7 healthcare centres for the management of rare adverse events following immunisation, according to the ministry.

Why HPV vaccination matters

Persistent infection with certain high-risk types of HPV is responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancer cases, and cervical cancer remains an important cause of cancer illness and death among women in India. The ministry said more than 800 million HPV vaccine doses have been administered worldwide, and that vaccinating girls at 14 is intended to provide protection well before potential exposure to the virus.

What happens next

The health ministry said it will keep working with state governments, district administrations, schools and communities to reach the remaining eligible girls and close coverage gaps. Parents and guardians of eligible 14-year-old girls are encouraged to visit their nearest designated government health facility or use the U-WIN platform to book a vaccination slot.

key_takeaways: India administered over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses in under nine months.
The campaign targets 1.2 crore 14-year-old girls annually.

Six states achieved 100% coverage of their target populations.
Vaccination is free, voluntary, and requires parental consent.
